boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Mobile Bay record (August 2-23, 1864) in Operations in Mobile Bay [August 1864]. The frozen interval spans the landing on Dauphin Island, the passage of the forts and the naval battle of August 5, the evacuation of Fort Powell, the surrender of Fort Gaines and the siege and surrender of Fort Morgan; these phases are kept within the one record and not split or added to other records. The 1865 Mobile Campaign is a separate campaign. Campaign-wide returns and multi-action loss totals are context, not assigned to one phase. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Farragut's fleet of 14 wooden ships and 4 monitors with army forces, against Buchanan's flotilla of three gunboats and an ironclad and the Morgan, Gaines and Powell garrisons; the live field reads zero. NPS says Farragut's fleet of eighteen ships entered the bay; Page says the fleet that moved up to pass Fort Morgan was twenty-three men-of-war, four of them monitors. Mahan lists four monitors in the starboard column and the wooden ships of the port column with their tonnage and guns, describes Buchanan's squadron as the ram Tennessee and three paddle-wheel gunboats, and says Granger had not men enough to attack both forts at once. Page gives his Fort Morgan garrison as some 400 effective during the siege.
claims.rationale: Ship counts, an army limitation and one garrison figure for different phases; no matched return. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Mahan says the main ship channel skirted Mobile Point and narrowed to a little under two thousand yards, that Fort Morgan commanded it while Gaines was too distant to count for much, and that a triple line of torpedoes left an opening not much over one hundred yards from the beach for blockade-runners. Page says the fort's brick walls proved easily penetrable and that the enemy could fire on it from every point of the compass.
claims.rationale: Ground and works described by a history and an interested report; no map verification. The works and obstructions predate the attack, but the phase is left unresolved.

claims.value: Mahan says Farragut took charge in person and turned the Hartford past the Brooklyn over the torpedo line, and that Buchanan directed the ram's battery in person until wounded. Page says he rejected Farragut's and Granger's joint demand and condemned Anderson's surrender of Gaines. The frozen commanders are Admiral Franklin Buchanan, Brigadier General Richard L. Page, Rear Admiral David G. Farragut and Major General Gordon Granger; the live page lists Farragut as Admiral and misspells Buchanan.
claims.rationale: Command roles from a history and an interested report; the listed commanders do not receive automatic sole credit, and the live rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Mahan says Fort Powell was evacuated the night of the 5th, Gaines surrendered the day after the 6th, and Fort Morgan surrendered on the 23rd; Page says the Union flag rose over Gaines on the morning of the 8th and that he capitulated at 2 p.m. on the 23rd. NPS says the city remained uncaptured. The live page files the record under Burbridge's Raid into Southwest Virginia, which conflicts with the frozen campaign and is not adopted.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,822 (US 322; CS 1,500); the live field reads 1,827 (US 327; CS 1,500). Mahan gives the Tennessee's loss as 2 killed and 10 wounded and the Union fleet's as 52 killed and 170 wounded, says 21 of the Tecumseh's complement of over a hundred were saved, and gives the Selma's loss as five killed and ten wounded. Page says the fort's casualties were slight on August 5 and unusually small in the siege; his lists are marked not found.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Granger's report (No. 4), Canby's dispatches (read, not selected), Maury's, Williams's, Buchanan's and the other army and naval reports in Volume XXXIX Part 1, Farragut's report in the Official Records of the Navies, and the prisoner counts for Forts Gaines and Morgan remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family (the NPS battle page plus the frozen Arnold rows). A. T. Mahan's The Gulf and Inland Waters (Scribner, 1883; Project Gutenberg transcription of the 1898 London printing) is a retrospective naval history by a Union naval officer, registered earlier for other engagements; its Mobile Bay chapter compiles its times from the logs and reports and quotes Farragut and Buchanan, so it is not independent of the naval reports. Page's August 6-30, 1864 reports to Maury (Official Records Series I, Volume XXXIX, Part 1, No. 14) are one family of interested Confederate accounts. The Official Records volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
